title: Polynomial formulas versus linear circuits
formal:
Does there exist a family of total Boolean functions \(f_n:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\), for integers \(n\ge1\), such that
\[S(f_n)=O(n)\qquad\text{but}\qquad L(f_n)\notin n^{O(1)}?\]
Here \(S\) is minimum bounded-fan-in De Morgan circuit gate count and \(L\) is minimum De Morgan formula leaf count. Both are nonuniform and require exact correctness on every input. Precisely, the question asks for one family and a finite constant \(C>0\) satisfying \(S(f_n)\le Cn\) for all \(n\ge1\), while
\[\forall k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \forall N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \exists n\ge N:\quad L(f_n)>n^k.\]
This is the source's absence-of-any-polynomial-upper-bound claim. It does not silently strengthen that claim to a lower bound beating each polynomial at every sufficiently large length.
why: Circuits can reuse intermediate values and formulas must duplicate the computation when it is needed again. This question asks whether reuse can turn a task requiring superpolynomial tree size into a circuit of only linear size. It isolates a fundamental limitation of formulas while allowing the circuit computation to have unrestricted depth.
status_note: Conjecture 5.11 and the source’s size definitions were checked on 2026-09-14, together with Filmus–Meir–Tal’s published Theorem 1.1 and introductory status discussion and Chukhin–Kulikov–Mihajlin’s STACS 2025 introduction. A bounded search through this date found no matching superpolynomial formula separation for a linear-size circuit family or a contrary universal simulation. The source-open status has these literature-check limits; the cited proofs have not been independently formalized.

importance.reason: Separates computation with reuse from formula computation, a basic structural distinction in circuit complexity.

sentences: The conjecture asks for Boolean functions with linear-size circuits but no polynomial-size formulas.
Circuits may reuse intermediate results, while formulas have a tree structure and count repeated variable occurrences separately.
The computational basis is binary AND and OR with unary negation, and correctness is exact on every input.
The nonuniform separation is equivalent to NC-one being strictly smaller than P/poly, and arbitrarily large violating lengths are sufficient.
Known nearly cubic gaps and recent composition results do not yet give the required superpolynomial separation.

definitions:
A Boolean circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with designated input nodes for \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) and one designated output. Every computational gate is binary AND, binary OR, or unary NOT. Inputs may also supply the constant bits zero and one. Each node carries one bit, which is evaluated by applying its assigned operation to the incoming values. Fan-out and depth are unrestricted, and a gate value can be reused several times. The output can be an input, a constant or a computed gate. Size is the number of computational gates; input and constant nodes and wires are not charged. The circuit must output \(f_n(x)\) on every \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). No parity or arbitrary truth-table gate is a primitive, and no random or promise-only correctness is allowed. \(S(f_n)\) is the minimum such size.

A formula is a finite rooted tree with binary AND/OR or unary NOT internal nodes and input-variable or constant leaves. Each occurrence of an input in this tree is separate; an internal computation cannot feed two parent nodes. The size of a formula is the number of variable-leaf occurrences, as in the source. Constant leaves are free; an optimum for a nonconstant function can eliminate constant subformulas. One may equivalently place all NOT operations directly on variables by De Morgan's laws, leaving the leaf count unchanged. Negated and unnegated occurrences of the same variable are each counted. \(L(f_n)\) is the minimum leaf count over formulas computing the function exactly. Constant functions have \(L=0\), and a literal has \(L=1\).

The sequence of functions, and the optimal circuits and formulas at different lengths, need not have an efficiently computable description. In particular this card does not impose an extra polynomial-time evaluator or uniform circuit-generation algorithm on the family. The source's conjecture is stated using its nonuniform size measures. A family with such extra uniformity would also qualify if it has the required sizes.

The same constant \(C\) bounds circuit size at every length. Allowing finitely many exceptions would be equivalent, since increasing \(C\) absorbs them. The formula condition is equivalent to saying that there do not exist constants \(D>0\), integer \(k\ge1\) and onset \(N\) with \(L(f_n)\le Dn^k\) for all \(n\ge N\). Thus arbitrarily large violating lengths may depend on the polynomial exponent; the family itself may not. The target asserts no particular exponential or quasipolynomial lower-bound rate.

The two minima compare computations of the same single-output function. Linear circuit size does not bound circuit depth by a logarithm. A size separation using unbounded-fan-in threshold gates, only monotone formulas, or a growing number of outputs is a different statement.

The existence claim is equivalent to \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\subsetneq\mathrm{P/poly}\) for nonuniform Boolean circuit families. Here \(\mathrm{P/poly}\) means \(S(f_n)\le a(n+1)^b\) for some fixed positive integers \(a,b\), and \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) means a family of binary De Morgan circuits of depth at most \(d\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) for one constant \(d\); such circuits can be taken polynomial in size. No uniform generation is required in either class. Polynomial-size formulas and logarithmic-depth circuits are equivalent by formula balancing and expansion of a bounded-depth circuit into a tree.

The restriction to linear circuit size does not change this family-existence question. A separating polynomial-size family can be regarded, at lengths \(N_n=a(n+1)^b\), as a function of \(N_n\) variables that ignores the extra variables; at other lengths set the function to a constant. The circuit bound becomes linear, whereas a polynomial formula bound in \(N_n\) would give a polynomial formula bound in \(n\). This is a comparison of nonuniform families and retains the arbitrarily-large-length quantifiers. Conversely, a linear-size family is already in \(\mathrm{P/poly}\). Thus an answer to the equality question has the opposite Boolean polarity from the separation question in this card.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed family-existence claim. A positive answer must specify or mathematically establish the existence of one family satisfying both the single linear circuit bound and failure of every polynomial formula bound. A nonconstructive family can qualify; no efficient generator is part of the target. A negative answer must show that every family with a uniform linear circuit-size constant has some polynomial formula-size bound, whose exponent and coefficient may depend on that family. Proving only one fixed polynomial separation, even with a large exponent, or refuting one candidate family does not settle the question.

context_blocks.text: Theorem 5.10 records families with linear-size circuits and nearly cubic formula lower bounds. Conjecture 5.11 asks for a qualitative increase beyond every fixed polynomial, not a further fixed-power improvement.

The 2023 paper proves nearly cubic De Morgan formula bounds for a family already computable by polynomial-size constant-depth unbounded-fan-in formulas. This strengthens the class of target functions for a known lower-bound scale; its Theorem 1.1 does not state the superpolynomial separation requested here.

The source connects its conjecture to questions about formula size under block composition. The related KRW card records a particular formula-size composition statement. This connection is contextual; the present target is stated directly in terms of the two computational size measures.

The STACS 2025 paper continues to describe super-logarithmic formula-depth lower bounds as a major open challenge. Its result is for a strengthened communication relation, and the authors explicitly distinguish it from a formula lower bound for ordinary composition.

Open Problem 8.3 in the Rao–Yehudayoff draft asks whether every polynomial-size circuit family has logarithmic-depth circuits. Formula balancing and polynomial padding give precisely the equivalence recorded in the definitions. The former active card TCS-6712 is consolidated here, preserving its source question rather than retaining two benchmark entries for opposite polarities of the same proposition.

Amarilli’s companion question asks more broadly whether the known nearly cubic circuit/formula gap can be improved. That broader quantitative question motivated the earlier consolidation, but a fixed-power improvement alone would not meet this card’s superpolynomial target.

community_reviews.original_text: This is the same question as whether boolean formulas have polynomial size circuits.
community_reviews.response: The duplicate was already consolidated into TCS-0019. The nontrivial direction is whether polynomial-size circuits have polynomial-size formulas (equivalently nonuniform NC1 = P/poly); formulas themselves are already circuits. The original note is retained here with its former card ID.
